notes:
Lead: Maya S. (AE) — strong ecomm background.
Key problem: seasonal search spikes (Black Fri/Cyber Mon) 6–8x baseline qps; current infra (managed search + on-prem reranker) costs spike >3x.
POC scope: evaluate Redwood Dedicated and Private for 24/7 baseline + burst policy; measure end-to-end cost per query (embedding lookup + top-k reranker) and p95 latency under burst.
Data size: ~120M product SKUs; metadata + images; embeddings update cadence: nightly for new SKUs, hourly for price/availability tags.
Reranking approach: hybrid retrieval — sparse first (BM25) -> embed candidate lookup (vector store) -> neural reranker on top-50. Customer wants neural reranker only at top-50 to control cost.
Targets: p95 tail <=120ms for query path (cold vs warmed cache); production cost per user query target <$0.002 (aiming for $0.0015).
Model preferences: open embeddings (high-dim float16 -> quantized candidate), smaller reranker tuned for relevance (prefer Llama-2 family finetuned or open re-ranker). They want Redwood to recommend quantization + batching profiles.
Security: require SSO (SAML), KMS for key control, audit logs retained 2y, EMEA data residency for EU customers.
Quote from CTO: "We need predictable dollars/txn — spikes should not ruin GA margin."
Artifacts shared: pricing sensitivity spreadsheet, sample product dump (1.2M rows subset), security questionnaire partial.
